I am 69 years old, and I have farmed this land in Quzhou for 50 years. My wife and I work our 10.1 mu together — just the two of us now. It is early spring, and my winter wheat is already in the ground from last October. I can see it greening up after the winter dormancy.

For my wheat, I planted it with my own saved seeds — I have been using this variety for many years and I trust it. At sowing last autumn I applied compound fertilizer as a base, and now at green-up I will topdress with urea. I usually put down about 24 kg of nitrogen per mu in total, split between the base and the topdressing. The compound fertilizer also gives me phosphorus and potassium — roughly 18 kg of phosphorus and 4 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times from my well: once now at green-up, once at jointing, and once at heading. Pumping costs money, but wheat cannot go thirsty at those stages. I will spray twice for weeds and insects. If the weather does not turn bad, I expect about 475 kg per mu.

For my summer maize, I plant Denghai 605, a hybrid seed I buy fresh every year. After I harvest the wheat in early June, there is almost no time to waste — the turnaround is very tight. I do not till much for maize; I plant it right after the wheat comes off to catch the season. I apply compound fertilizer at planting, giving me about 14 kg of nitrogen, 3 kg of phosphorus, and 3 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate once, maybe a second time if July is very dry. I spray three times to control insects and weeds. I expect about 640 kg per mu from the maize.

I have been running this wheat-maize rotation for decades. I know every corner of these 10.1 mu. I do not need to change what works.
